title: The Problem-Solving Toolbox
topic: Pick a tool, solve with it, and check a second way

items.q: Ali has 12 pens. Mei has 4 fewer pens than Ali. How many pens do they have in all?
items.hint: Draw a strip. Find Mei first. Then add the two strips.
steps: Mei has 12 take away 4, which is 8 pens.

slips.say: That is Mei. Add the two strips for the total.

tpl.q: Ali has {a} pens. Mei has {b} fewer pens than Ali. How many pens do they have in all?
tpl.hint: Draw a strip. Find Mei first. Then add the two strips.
steps: {a} and Mei's pens make the total.

items.q: A row has 2 beads. Each next row has 3 more beads. How many beads are in the 5th row?
items.hint: Make a table. Add 3 each time.

slips.say: That is the 6th row. Row 1 is 2: count the rows.

tpl.q: A row has {s} beads. Each next row has {e} more beads. How many beads are in the {n|ord} row?
tpl.hint: Make a table. Add {e} each time.

items.q: I think of a number. I add 6 and get 15. What is my number?

slips.say: Do not add. Work backwards: take 6 away.

tpl.q: I think of a number. I add {a} and get {t}. What is my number?

items.q: 3 pens cost $9. All the pens cost the same. How much does 1 pen cost?
items.hint: Find one first. Share $9 into 3 equal parts.

slips.say: Do not add. Share the money into equal parts.

tpl.q: {k} pens cost ${p}. All the pens cost the same. How much does 1 pen cost?
tpl.hint: Find one first. Share ${p} into {k} equal parts.
steps: Each part is the price of 1 pen.

items.q: A number take away 7 is 10. Which tool fits best?
items.hint: We know the end, not the start.

slips.say: No pattern grows here. We know the end, not the start.

items.q: 4 boxes hold 24 shells. All the boxes hold the same number. How many shells do 7 boxes hold?
items.hint: Find one first. Then count 7 groups.
steps: 24 shared into 4 boxes is 6 shells in 1 box.

slips.say: That is 1 box. Now find 7 boxes.

tpl.q: {k} boxes hold {t} shells. All the boxes hold the same number. How many shells do {m} boxes hold?
tpl.hint: Find one first. Then count {m} groups.
steps: {t} shared into {k} boxes is the number in 1 box.

items.q: I think of a number. I add 9. Then I take away 4. I get 20. What is my number?
items.hint: Work backwards. Undo the last step first.
steps: Undo the take away 4: 20 and 4 make 24.

slips.say: Do not add 9 again. Undo it with a take away.

tpl.q: I think of a number. I add {a}. Then I take away {b}. I get {r}. What is my number?
tpl.hint: Work backwards. Undo the last step first.
steps: Undo the take away {b}: {r} and {b} make a number.

items.q: Find every way to pay 30¢ with 10¢ coins and 5¢ coins. Which tool helps most?
steps: A list finds every way, one by one.

slips.say: We do not know an end. We want every way.

items.q: Amelia has 3 times as many shells as Wei. They have 24 shells in all. How many shells does Wei have?
steps: Wei has 1 part and Amelia has 3 parts.
24 shared into 4 is 6 shells for Wei.

slips.say: That shares 24 into 3 parts. Count the parts of Wei and Amelia together.

tpl.q: Amelia has 3 times as many shells as Wei. They have {t} shells in all. How many shells does Wei have?
steps: Wei has 1 part and Amelia has 3 parts.
{t} shared into 4 is {ans} shells for Wei.

items.q: Amelia has 3 times as many shells as Wei. They have 24 shells in all. How many shells does Amelia have?
items.hint: Find Wei first. Then count 3 parts.
steps: Amelia has 3 parts of 6, which is 18 shells.

slips.say: That is Wei. Amelia has 3 times as many.

tpl.q: Amelia has 3 times as many shells as Wei. They have {t} shells in all. How many shells does Amelia have?
tpl.hint: Find Wei first. Then count 3 parts.
steps: {t} shared into 4 equal parts is Wei's shells.
Amelia has 3 parts of that number.

items.q: Pick a tool card and write a problem for it. Solve it, then check it a second way.
items.hint: Pick the tool first. Then think of a story.
steps: Write a short story with numbers and a question.
Solve it, then check it another way.

items.q: A child writes 70 − 30 = 40. Add back to check. What is 40 + 30?
items.hint: Add the answer and the number you took away.
steps: We get back to 70, so the take away is right.

slips.say: 10 is the gap. To check, add the answer and the number taken away.

tpl.q: A child writes {s} − {b} = {a}. Add back to check. What is {a} + {b}?
tpl.hint: Add the answer and the number you took away.
steps: We get back to {s}, so the take away is right.

items.q: A child forgot the ten when adding. The child wrote 39 + 24 = 53. What is the right answer?
items.hint: The ones make more than 9. Do not forget the ten.

slips.say: 53 is the answer with the ten missing. Add the ten.

tpl.q: A child forgot the ten when adding. The child wrote {a} + {b} = {w}. What is the right answer?
tpl.hint: The ones make more than 9. Do not forget the ten.
steps: Add the ones. They make more than 9.
Write the ones and add the ten.
